investigation.title: Screen-Space Reflections
investigation.summary: How Godot's Forward+ renderer reflects what is on screen: a depth pyramid, a ray marched through it, last frame's colour, and a blur by roughness.
investigation.footer: Godot 4.7.2-stable, read from its source. Every claim cites a file, a symbol, and a line.
investigation.demo_hint: Drag to orbit; the dock's sliders set the Environment's SSR settings and the materials.
hints.ssr: The Environment's SSR settings, as Godot pushes them to the passes.
hints.surface: The materials SSR reflects in, and Godot's roughness limiter.
help.floorRoughness: The floor's material roughness. SSR traces below 0.7 and fades out from 0.6.
help.ssrEnabled: Environment.ssr_enabled: whether the passes run and the opaque pass blends their result in.
help.ssrMaxSteps: Environment.ssr_max_steps: the trace's iterations per pixel (default 64).
help.ssrFadeIn: Environment.ssr_fade_in: the exponent of the fade over the ray's screen length near its start (default 0.15).
help.ssrFadeOut: Environment.ssr_fade_out: the exponent of the fade toward one screen length (default 2).
help.ssrDepthTolerance: Environment.ssr_depth_tolerance: how far behind a surface a ray may pass at level 0, in view-space units (default 0.5).
help.roughnessLimiter: The project's screen-space roughness limiter (on by default): roughness widened where the normal changes across a pixel.
pass.ssrPrepassFS: The depth pre-pass: depth and the normal-roughness buffer (the encoded view-space normal and the roughness).
pass.ssrForwardFS: The opaque pass: the sky's reflection, specular occlusion, SSR blended in by its validity, then the environment BRDF.
pass.ssrBestFit: The best-fit normal table, made once: for each direction, the length that quantizes to eight bits with the least error.
pass.ssrDownsample: SSR Downsample: half-size depth (the nearest of each 2 x 2) and the winner's normal-roughness.
pass.ssrHiz: SSR HI-Z: each level of the depth pyramid the nearest depth of four texels of the level before.
pass.ssrTrace: SSR Main: one ray per half-size pixel, marched through the pyramid; its validity, last frame's colour, and a blur level.
pass.ssrFilter: SSR Roughness Filter: each level of the reflection's mips a blur of the level before.
pass.ssrResolve: SSR Resolve: back to full size, four half-size taps weighted by depth, normal, and roughness.
pass.ssrCopyLastFrame: Copy Framebuffer for SSIL/SSR: this frame's colour, kept at half size for the next frame's trace.

help.skyReflection: Environment.reflected_light_source: the sky as the reflection SSR covers (Godot's default with a sky), or Disabled (none: only what SSR finds).
help.floorMetallic: The floor material's metallic: a metal's f0 is its albedo, so its reflection is stronger (the lab's other objects are dielectric, f0 0.04).

help.pickX: The picked SSR pixel's column (half size); below 0, the pixel P in front of the teapot.
help.pickY: The picked SSR pixel's row (half size); below 0, the pixel P in front of the teapot.
help.pickWidth: The SSR buffer width (half size) the picked pixel was chosen at; 0, the current one. At another width, the pick moves to the same direction from the camera.
help.pickHeight: The SSR buffer height (half size) the picked pixel was chosen at; 0, the current one. At another height, the pick moves to the same direction from the camera.
help.traceStep: How many of the trace's iterations are shown, from the first.

controls.field: The depth map as a height field
hints.field: Each SSR texel a column as tall as it is near (reversed depth): a pyramid level keeps the tallest of each 2 x 2, and the ray marches over the columns.
help.fieldShow: Fades the height field in over the room, on a dark ground: 0 the room alone, 1 the field alone.
help.fieldMorph: 0: the depth map flat, as the screen shows it; 1: tilted back, each texel risen into its column.
help.fieldLevel: The pyramid level of the columns; between two levels, each 2 x 2 rises to its tallest and the four merge into one.
help.fieldZoom: 0: the whole field; 1: a close window around P.
help.fieldTurn: Turns the tilted field about its own up, in degrees.
help.profileShow: Shows the trace as a cross-section along the ray: across, t from P; up, reversed depth. The level's cells stand as bars; the step's cell is lit, with where the ray leaves it and where it reaches its depth.
help.fieldTilt: How far the risen field lies back, in degrees: 0 seen from straight above, 85 almost edge-on. Dragging the field turns and tilts it; the camera that renders the depth map stays where it is.
